entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen32318" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen32319" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32320" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32320" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32319" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32321" type="x-p"/> The prophet having formerly predicted the ruin of Edom, the same with Seir, (<reference osisRef="Eze.25.12">Eze 25:12</reference>), now resumes and pursues the subject at greater length, intimating, as did also Isaiah, (<reference osisRef="Isa.21.11">Isa 21:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.21.12">Isa 21:12</reference>), that though other nations should recover their liberty after the fall of the Babylonian monarchy, the Edomites should continue in bondage for their very despiteful behavior towards the children of Israel in the day of their calamity, <reference osisRef="Eze.35.1-Eze.35.15">Eze 35:1-15</reference>.
entries.content_plain: Introduction The prophet having formerly predicted the ruin of Edom, the same with Seir, ( Eze 25:12 ), now resumes and pursues the subject at greater length, intimating, as did also Isaiah, ( Isa 21:11 , Isa 21:12 ), that though other nations should recover their liberty after the fall of the Babylonian monarchy, the Edomites should continue in bondage for their very despiteful behavior towards the children of Israel in the day of their calamity, Eze 35:1-15 .

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen32321" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32322" type="x-p"/> Set thy face against Mount Seir - That is, against the Edomites. This prophecy was probably delivered about the time of the preceding, and before the destruction of Idumea by Nebuchadnezzar, which took place about five years after. <div eID="gen32322" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32323" type="x-p"/> Calmet supposes that two destructions of Idumea are here foretold; one by Nebuchadnezzar, and the other by the Jews after their return from their captivity.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen32324" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32325" type="x-p"/> A perpetual hatred - The Edomites were the descendants of Esau; the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob. Both these were brothers; and between them there was contention even in the womb, and they lived generally in a state of enmity. Their descendants kept up the ancient feud: but the Edomites were implacable; they had not only a rooted but perpetual enmity to the Israelites, harassing and distressing them by all possible means; and they seized the opportunity, when the Israelites were most harassed by other enemies, to make inroads upon them, and cut them off wherever they found them. <div eID="gen32325" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32326" type="x-p"/> To afflict the afflicted is cruel. This is scarcely of man, bad as he is. He must be possessed by the malignant spirit of the devil, when he wounds the wounded, insults over the miseries of the afflicted, and seeks opportunities to add affliction to those who are already under the rod of God.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen32326" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32327" type="x-p"/> Blood shall pursue thee - Thou lovest blood, and thou shalt have blood. It is said that Cyrus and two hundred thousand men were slain in an ambush by Thomyris, queen of the Scythians, and that she cut ok his head, and threw it into a vessel filled with blood, with this severe sarcasm: - <div eID="gen32327" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32328" type="x-p"/> Satia te sanguine quem sitisti, Cyre. "O Cyrus, now satisfy thyself with blood." <div eID="gen32328" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32329" type="x-p"/> Hence, the figure: - "Sarcasmus, with this biting taunt doth kill: <div eID="gen32329" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32330" type="x-p"/> Cyrus, thy thirst was blood, now drink thy fill."

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen32331" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32332" type="x-p"/> These two nations - Israel and Judah. The Idumeans thought of conquering and possessing both; and they would have succeeded, but only the Lord was there; and this spoiled their projects, and blasted their hopes.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen32335" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32336" type="x-p"/> So will I do unto thee - Others shall rejoice in thy downfall as thou hast rejoiced at their downfall. <div eID="gen32336" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32337" type="x-p"/> This whole chapter strongly inculcates this maxim: Do as thou wouldst be done by; and what thou wouldst not have done to thee, do not to others. And from it we learn that every man may, in some sort, be said to make his own temporal good or evil; for as he does to others, God will take care to do to him, whether it be evil or good, weal or wo. Would you not be slandered or backbitten? Then do not slander nor backbite. Wouldst thou wish to live in peace? Then do not disturb the peace of others. Be merciful, and thou shalt obtain mercy.  <chapter eID="Ezek.35"/> <div eID="gen32337" type="x-p"/>
